newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 2.14 pct up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 2.14 pct up on foreign buying.

text.p: Sustained foreign buying of blue-chip banks and finance stocks spurred a 2.14 percent market rally on Thursday, brokers said.

"Market sentiment improved, helped by selective foreign buying which was different from last week when they bought across the board. I think they found Thai stocks cheaper after the baht exchange rate system was changed to a managed float," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index advanced 13.62 points to 649.33 on 8.06 billion baht turnover.
Foreign investors have returned to the Thai bourse since Thailand floated its baht in a de facto devaluation on July 2.
"Foreigners are watching how far the rally would be sustained and that prompt them to be selective today," said Payuha.
Most key sectors advanced. The banking sector led the gainers rising 2.41 percent, the communication sector surged 5.20 percent, and the finance sector rallied 5.58 percent.
The SET-50 index gained 1.26 points to 49.19.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising three baht to 174, United Communication gained four to 108, and National Finance advanced 2.50 to 27.75.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue advancing on Friday on expected foreign bargain hunting.
